[Tool call] Write
  path: c:\Users\chong\AI Studio\aimediatank-azure\azure-functions\video-processor\ProcessVideo\index.ts
  contents: import { AzureFunction, Context, HttpRequest } from "@azure/functions";
import { BlobServiceClient } from "@azure/storage-blob";
import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";
import * as ffmpeg from "fluent-ffmpeg";
import * as fs from "fs";
import * as path from "path";
import * as os from "os";

const prisma = new PrismaClient();

interface ProcessVideoRequest {
  mediaId: string;
  blobUrl: string;
  cropTop: number;
  cropBottom: number;
  cropLeft: number;
  cropRight: number;
}

// Parse Azure blob URL to get container and blob name
function parseAzureUrl(url: string): { containerName: string; blobName: string } | null {
  try {
    const u = new URL(url);
    const parts = u.pathname.replace(/^\/+/, "").split("/").filter(Boolean);
    if (parts.length >= 2) {
      return { containerName: parts[0], blobName: parts.slice(1).join("/") };
    }
    return null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

// Get file extension from URL or default to .mp4
function getFileExtension(url: string): string {
  const parsed = parseAzureUrl(url);
  if (parsed) {
    const ext = path.extname(parsed.blobName).toLowerCase();
    if (ext) return ext;
  }
  return ".mp4";
}

const httpTrigger: AzureFunction = async function (
  context: Context,
  req: HttpRequest
): Promise<void> {
  context.log("Video processing function triggered");

  try {
    const body: ProcessVideoRequest = req.body;

    if (!body.mediaId || !body.blobUrl) {
      context.res = {
        status: 400,
        body: { error: "Missing required fields: mediaId, blobUrl" },
      };
      return;
    }

    const { mediaId, blobUrl, cropTop, cropBottom, cropLeft, cropRight } = body;

    context.log(`Processing video for media ${mediaId}`);
    context.log(`Crop params: top=${cropTop}, bottom=${cropBottom}, left=${cropLeft}, right=${cropRight}`);

    // Update status to processing
    await prisma.media.update({
      where: { id: mediaId },
      data: { processingStatus: "processing" },
    });

    // Get blob client
    const connectionString = process.env.AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING;
    if (!connectionString) {
      throw new Error("AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING not configured");
    }

    const blobServiceClient = BlobServiceClient.fromConnectionString(connectionString);
    const parsed = parseAzureUrl(blobUrl);

    if (!parsed) {
      throw new Error(`Invalid blob URL: ${blobUrl}`);
    }

    const containerClient = blobServiceClient.getContainerClient(parsed.containerName);
    const blobClient = containerClient.getBlobClient(parsed.blobName);

    // Download the original video to temp file
    const tempDir = os.tmpdir();
    const inputExt = getFileExtension(blobUrl);
    const inputPath = path.join(tempDir, `input_${mediaId}${inputExt}`);
    const outputPath = path.join(tempDir, `output_${mediaId}.mp4`);

    context.log(`Downloading blob to ${inputPath}`);
    const downloadResponse = await blobClient.download();
    const writeStream = fs.createWriteStream(inputPath);

    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      const readable = downloadResponse.readableStreamBody;
      if (!readable) {
        reject(new Error("No readable stream from blob"));
        return;
      }
      readable.pipe(writeStream);
      readable.on("end", () => resolve());
      readable.on("error", reject);
      writeStream.on("error", reject);
    });

    context.log("Download complete, starting FFmpeg processing");

    // Get video info to calculate crop dimensions
    const videoInfo = await new Promise<ffmpeg.FfprobeData>((resolve, reject) => {
      ffmpeg.ffprobe(inputPath, (err, info) => {
        if (err) reject(err);
        else resolve(info);
      });
    });

    const videoStream = videoInfo.streams.find((s) => s.codec_type === "video");
    if (!videoStream || !videoStream.width || !videoStream.height) {
      throw new Error("Could not determine video dimensions");
    }

    const originalWidth = videoStream.width;
    const originalHeight = videoStream.height;

    // Calculate crop dimensions
    const cropWidth = originalWidth - cropLeft - cropRight;
    const cropHeight = originalHeight - cropTop - cropBottom;

    if (cropWidth <= 0 || cropHeight <= 0) {
      throw new Error(`Invalid crop dimensions: ${cropWidth}x${cropHeight}`);
    }

    // Ensure even dimensions for video encoding
    const finalWidth = Math.floor(cropWidth / 2) * 2;
    const finalHeight = Math.floor(cropHeight / 2) * 2;

    context.log(`Cropping: ${originalWidth}x${originalHeight} -> ${finalWidth}x${finalHeight}`);
    context.log(`Crop filter: crop=${finalWidth}:${finalHeight}:${cropLeft}:${cropTop}`);

    // Process video with FFmpeg
    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      ffmpeg(inputPath)
        .videoFilters(`crop=${finalWidth}:${finalHeight}:${cropLeft}:${cropTop}`)
        .outputOptions([
          "-c:v libx264",
          "-preset fast",
          "-crf 23",
          "-c:a aac",
          "-b:a 192k",
          "-movflags +faststart",
        ])
        .output(outputPath)
        .on("start", (cmd) => context.log(`FFmpeg command: ${cmd}`))
        .on("progress", (progress) => {
          if (progress.percent) {
            context.log(`Processing: ${Math.round(progress.percent)}%`);
          }
        })
        .on("end", () => resolve())
        .on("error", (err) => reject(err))
        .run();
    });

    context.log("FFmpeg processing complete, uploading result");

    // Upload processed video with a new name
    const outputBlobName = parsed.blobName.replace(/\.[^.]+$/, "_cropped.mp4");
    const outputBlobClient = containerClient.getBlockBlobClient(outputBlobName);

    const processedBuffer = fs.readFileSync(outputPath);
    await outputBlobClient.upload(processedBuffer, processedBuffer.length, {
      blobHTTPHeaders: { blobContentType: "video/mp4" },
    });

    const newUrl = outputBlobClient.url;
    context.log(`Uploaded cropped video to: ${newUrl}`);

    // Update database with new URL and status
    await prisma.media.update({
      where: { id: mediaId },
      data: {
        url: newUrl,
        processingStatus: "completed",
        processingError: null,
      },
    });

    // Clean up temp files
    try {
      fs.unlinkSync(inputPath);
      fs.unlinkSync(outputPath);
    } catch {
      // Ignore cleanup errors
    }

    context.log(`Video processing completed for media ${mediaId}`);

    context.res = {
      status: 200,
      body: {
        success: true,
        mediaId,
        newUrl,
        dimensions: { width: finalWidth, height: finalHeight },
      },
    };
  } catch (error: any) {
    context.log.error("Video processing failed:", error);

    // Try to update the media record with error status
    try {
      const body: ProcessVideoRequest = req.body;
      if (body?.mediaId) {
        await prisma.media.update({
          where: { id: body.mediaId },
          data: {
            processingStatus: "failed",
            processingError: error.message || "Unknown error",
          },
        });
      }
    } catch {
      // Ignore update errors
    }

    context.res = {
      status: 500,
      body: {
        error: "Video processing failed",
        details: error.message,
      },
    };
  } finally {
    await prisma.$disconnect();
  }
};

export default httpTrigger;

  path: c:\Users\chong\AI Studio\aimediatank-azure\azure-functions\video-processor\README.md
  contents: # Video Processor Azure Function

This Azure Function handles backend video cropping using FFmpeg.

## Features

- Receives video crop parameters from the main app
- Downloads video from Azure Blob Storage
- Uses FFmpeg to crop the video
- Uploads the processed video back to Azure Blob Storage
- Updates the database with the new video URL

## Prerequisites

1. Azure Functions Core Tools
2. Node.js 18+
3. Azure subscription with:
   - Function App (Container-based deployment)
   - Storage Account
   - Access to the same database as the main app

## Local Development

1. Copy `local.settings.json.example` to `local.settings.json`
2. Fill in the required values:
   - `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING`: Your Azure Storage connection string
   - `DATABASE_URL`: PostgreSQL connection string

3. Install dependencies:
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```

4. Build TypeScript:
   ```bash
   npm run build
   ```

5. Run locally (requires FFmpeg installed):
   ```bash
   npm start
   ```

## Deployment

### Option 1: Azure Container Registry + Function App

1. Build the Docker image:
   ```bash
   docker build -t aimediatank-video-processor .
   ```

2. Tag and push to Azure Container Registry:
   ```bash
   az acr login --name <your-registry>
   docker tag aimediatank-video-processor <your-registry>.azurecr.io/aimediatank-video-processor:latest
   docker push <your-registry>.azurecr.io/aimediatank-video-processor:latest
   ```

3. Create Function App with container:
   ```bash
   az functionapp create \
     --name aimediatank-video-processor \
     --resource-group <your-resource-group> \
     --storage-account <your-storage-account> \
     --plan <your-app-service-plan> \
     --deployment-container-image-name <your-registry>.azurecr.io/aimediatank-video-processor:latest
   ```

4. Configure environment variables:
   ```bash
   az functionapp config appsettings set \
     --name aimediatank-video-processor \
     --resource-group <your-resource-group> \
     --settings \
       AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING="<connection-string>" \
       DATABASE_URL="<database-url>"
   ```

### Option 2: Premium Plan with Custom Handler

For better performance, use Azure Functions Premium Plan which supports longer execution times.

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING` | Azure Storage connection string |
| `AZURE_STORAGE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Blob container name (default: "media") |
| `DATABASE_URL` | PostgreSQL connection string for Prisma |

## API Endpoint

**POST** `/api/ProcessVideo`

Request body:
```json
{
  "mediaId": "uuid",
  "blobUrl": "https://storage.blob.core.windows.net/media/video.mp4",
  "cropTop": 50,
  "cropBottom": 50,
  "cropLeft": 0,
  "cropRight": 0
}
```

Response:
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "mediaId": "uuid",
  "newUrl": "https://storage.blob.core.windows.net/media/video_cropped.mp4",
  "dimensions": { "width": 1920, "height": 980 }
}
```

## Main App Configuration

Add the following environment variable to your main Next.js app:

```
AZURE_VIDEO_PROCESSING_URL=https://<function-app-name>.azurewebsites.net/api/ProcessVideo?code=<function-key>
```

Get the function key from Azure Portal → Function App → Functions → ProcessVideo → Function Keys.

## Summary: Backend Video Cropping Implementation

### What's Implemented:

**1. Database Schema Changes** (`prisma/schema.prisma`):
- Added `processingStatus`: `"none"` | `"pending"` | `"processing"` | `"completed"` | `"failed"`
- Added `processingError` for error messages
- Added `originalUrl` to store the pre-crop URL
- Added `cropTop`, `cropBottom`, `cropLeft`, `cropRight` fields
- Same fields added to `PendingUpload` model

**2. Upload Flow Changes** (`src/app/upload/page.tsx`):
- Videos with crop params skip client-side re-encoding
- Original file uploaded directly to Azure
- Crop parameters sent to backend APIs

**3. API Updates**:
- `/api/upload/complete` - stores crop params, triggers Azure Function
- `/api/stripe/upload-payment` - stores crop params in PendingUpload
- `/api/stripe/webhook` - handles crop params when converting pending to media

**4. Azure Function** (`azure-functions/video-processor/`):
- HTTP-triggered function with FFmpeg
- Downloads video from blob storage
- Crops using FFmpeg with specified parameters
- Uploads processed video with `_cropped.mp4` suffix
- Updates database with new URL and status

### Next Steps to Deploy:

1. **Run database migration** (on deployment):
   ```bash
   npx prisma migrate deploy
   ```

2. **Deploy the Azure Function**:
   - Build Docker image with FFmpeg
   - Push to Azure Container Registry
   - Create Function App
   - See `azure-functions/video-processor/README.md` for detailed instructions

3. **Configure environment variable** in main app:
   ```
   AZURE_VIDEO_PROCESSING_URL=https://<function-name>.azurewebsites.net/api/ProcessVideo?code=<function-key>
   ```

4. **Optional**: Update UI to show "Processing..." status for videos (pending task)

      // Validate crop area
      if (!cropArea || cropArea.width <= 0 || cropArea.height <= 0) {
        console.error('Invalid crop area:', cropArea)
        return null
      }
      
      const image = await createImage(imageSrc)
      console.log('Image loaded:', { naturalWidth: image.naturalWidth, naturalHeight: image.naturalHeight })
      
      const canvas = document.createElement('canvas')
      const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')
      if (!ctx) {
        console.error('Failed to get canvas 2d context')
        return null
      }

      // Ensure dimensions are integers and at least 1
      const width = Math.max(1, Math.round(cropArea.width))
      const height = Math.max(1, Math.round(cropArea.height))
      const x = Math.max(0, Math.round(cropArea.x))
      const y = Math.max(0, Math.round(cropArea.y))
      
      canvas.width = width
      canvas.height = height
      
      ctx.drawImage(
        image,
        x,
        y,
        width,
        height,
        0,
        0,
        width,
        height
      )

      return new Promise<File | null>((resolve) => {
        // Try toBlob first (modern browsers)
        try {
          canvas.toBlob(
            (blob) => {
              if (blob) {
                console.log('Canvas toBlob succeeded, size:', blob.size)
                resolve(new File([blob], 'cropped-image.jpg', { type: 'image/jpeg' }))
              } else {
                // Fallback to toDataURL for older browsers
                console.warn('toBlob returned null, trying toDataURL fallback')
                try {
                  const dataUrl = canvas.toDataURL('image/jpeg', 0.9)
                  const arr = dataUrl.split(',')
                  const mime = arr[0].match(/:(.*?);/)?.[1] || 'image/jpeg'
                  const bstr = atob(arr[1])
                  let n = bstr.length
                  const u8arr = new Uint8Array(n)
                  while (n--) {
                    u8arr[n] = bstr.charCodeAt(n)
                  }
                  const fallbackBlob = new Blob([u8arr], { type: mime })
                  resolve(new File([fallbackBlob], 'cropped-image.jpg', { type: 'image/jpeg' }))
                } catch (e) {
                  console.error('toDataURL fallback failed:', e)
                  resolve(null)
                }
              }
            },
            'image/jpeg',
            0.9
          )
        } catch (e) {
          console.error('toBlob threw error:', e)
          resolve(null)
        }
      })
    } catch (err) {
      console.error('getCroppedImageFile error:', err)
      return null
    }
  }

    new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const image = new Image()
      // Add crossOrigin for data URLs on some mobile browsers
      if (!url.startsWith('data:')) {
        image.crossOrigin = 'anonymous'
      }
      
      const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
        reject(new Error('Image load timeout'))
      }, 10000) // 10 second timeout
      
      image.onload = () => {
        clearTimeout(timeout)
        resolve(image)
      }
      image.onerror = (error) => {
        clearTimeout(timeout)
        reject(error)
      }
      image.src = url
    })

## Fixed: Mobile Crop Tool

The crop tool wasn't working on mobile because several state values weren't being properly set. Here's what I fixed:

### Issues Found:
1. **`mediaSize` not set on mobile** - The image `onLoad` event wasn't firing reliably on mobile Safari/Chrome
2. **`cropAreaPixels` calculation dependent on `mediaSize`** - Without mediaSize, no crop area was calculated
3. **`handleUseEdited` failing silently** - No error handling or fallbacks when crop data was missing

### Fixes Applied:

1. **Added useEffect to pre-load cropSource dimensions** - Ensures `mediaSize` is set even if the JSX image onLoad doesn't fire

2. **Added fallback calculation in `handleUseEdited`** - If `cropAreaPixels` isn't set but we have `cropInsets`, calculate it directly

3. **Improved `getCroppedImageFile`**:
   - Added `toDataURL` fallback for browsers where `toBlob` fails
   - Added validation for crop area dimensions
   - Added comprehensive error logging

4. **Improved `createImage`**:
   - Added 10-second timeout to prevent hanging
   - Added crossOrigin attribute for compatibility

5. **Multiple fallback strategies for `videoCrop`**:
   - Primary: Use `mediaSize` and `videoSize` with ratios
   - Fallback: Use `cropInsets` scaled to video dimensions

Please test the crop tool on mobile again. The console will now show detailed logs if anything goes wrong.

Done! Pushed to staging and main.

## Key Fix

The core issue was that `mediaSize` and `renderBox` weren't being set on mobile because they relied on the image `onLoad` event, which doesn't fire reliably on iOS/mobile browsers.

**The Fix:** Now `mediaSize` and `renderBox` are set **directly** when the video thumbnail is generated, rather than waiting for the img onLoad event:

1. `generateVideoThumbnail` now returns the thumbnail dimensions along with the file
2. When the thumbnail is generated, we immediately set `mediaSize` with the known dimensions
3. We also set a reasonable `renderBox` so `cropAreaPixels` can be calculated right away
4. This ensures all crop state is ready before the crop modal even opens

This bypasses the unreliable onLoad event entirely for videos.

Please test again on mobile - the crop tool should now properly apply the crop settings when you click "Upload Edit".

[Thinking] The user is reporting that the crop tool doesn't actually crop the video - it plays the original video at the end. This is expected based on the changes we made earlier for backend processing (Option 1 - Azure Functions with FFmpeg).

<user_query>
Verify this issue exists and fix it:

The removal of fallback calculations for video cropping can cause user-applied crops to be silently discarded. Previously, when `cropAreaPixels` was null but `mediaSize` was available, the code calculated `effectiveCropArea` from `cropInsets`. Additionally, if `mediaSize` was unavailable but `videoSize` and `cropInsets` existed, a secondary fallback would scale crop insets directly to video dimensions. Both fallbacks are now removed. If `cropAreaPixels` is null (which can happen on mobile where `mediaSize` may not be set reliably), `handleUseEdited` returns early without setting `videoCrop`, resulting in the original uncropped video being uploaded despite the user's cropping intent. @src/app/upload/page.tsx:431-444 @src/app/upload/page.tsx:413-417

assistant:
[Thinking] **Confirming crop flow**

The crop selection happens client-side, while actual cropping and re-encoding occur on the backend if the video processing URL is configured; otherwise, cropping is skipped.
Short answer: **crop selection is client‑side, and re‑encoding is done by the backend Azure Function** (when `AZURE_VIDEO_PROCESSING_URL` is configured).

Details:
- The UI computes `videoCrop` client‑side from the crop tool.
- For videos with crop, the client **uploads the original file** and sends `cropParams` to the backend.
- The backend marks the media as `processing` and triggers the Azure Function to crop/re‑encode.

If `AZURE_VIDEO_PROCESSING_URL` is not set, the backend logs a warning and the crop won’t be applied.

<user_query>
what is the problem doing both at backend azure?
</user_query>

assistant:
[Thinking] **Explaining crop handling trade-offs**

Cropping requires original upload plus crop parameters since the backend handles crop and encoding; this causes latency, higher costs, infrastructure complexity, queuing delays, larger uploads, and challenges providing user feedback during processing.
Doing both crop **and** re‑encode on backend Azure is totally workable. The trade‑offs/problems are mostly operational, not technical:

- **Latency & UX**: Users won’t see final cropped media immediately; you need a processing state/queue and a UI that updates later.
- **Cost**: Azure Functions + storage I/O + FFmpeg time can get expensive at scale.
- **Throughput & limits**: Function timeouts, CPU/memory limits, and cold starts can slow or fail large videos.
- **Error handling**: You need retries, failure states, and cleanup of partial outputs.
- **Original upload size**: You still upload the full file, so bandwidth/time remains high.
- **Monitoring & observability**: You need logs, alerts, and job tracking to debug failed crops.

If you’re okay with those, backend‑only is actually the most reliable for consistent quality and mobile compatibility.

<user_query>
what is the benefits for that
</user_query>

assistant:
If we do **both crop + re‑encode on the Azure backend**, the benefits are:

- **Consistent results** across devices and browsers (no mobile GPU/codec quirks).
- **Better quality control** with FFmpeg (stable bitrate, resolution, keyframes).
- **No client CPU load** → faster UI, fewer crashes/overheating on phones.
- **Single source of truth**: only one final file, no mismatch between preview vs. upload.
- **Easier debugging** with centralized logs and deterministic processing.
- **Future‑proofing**: you can change encoding profiles without updating clients.

The trade‑off is you must show a processing state until the new URL is ready.

<user_query>
is Docker container new azure resource i need to add?
</user_query>

assistant:
Not necessarily. You **can** deploy the Function App as a Docker container, but it’s optional.

Two options:

**A) Docker container (recommended for FFmpeg)**
- You build/push the container image and set the Function App to use that image.
- You’ll need **Azure Container Registry (ACR)** (or Docker Hub). That is a new resource if you don’t already have one.

**B) Zip deploy (no container)**
- No new ACR resource.
- But you must ensure **FFmpeg is available** in the Function runtime (often not), so this can fail.

For video processing with FFmpeg, **Docker is the reliable path**. If you don’t have ACR yet, we should create it.

<user_query>
Let's do deploy the Function App as a Docker container
</user_query>

assistant:
[Thinking] **Outlining concise Azure deployment steps**

I'm preparing clear, step-by-step guidance to create an Azure Container Registry, build and push a container image, then configure the existing Function App to use the custom container with necessary environment variables and share the app URL after deployment.
Got it. We’ll deploy the **video-processor** as a Docker container.

## 1) Create an Azure Container Registry (ACR)
If you don’t already have one:
```
az acr create \
  --resource-group aimediatank-function_group \
  --name <yourACRName> \
  --sku Basic
```

## 2) Build + push the Docker image
From the repo root:
```
cd azure-functions/video-processor
az acr login --name <yourACRName>

docker build -t <yourACRName>.azurecr.io/aimediatank-video-processor:latest .
docker push <yourACRName>.azurecr.io/aimediatank-video-processor:latest
```

## 3) Configure the Function App to use the image
```
az functionapp config container set \
  --name aimediatank-function \
  --resource-group aimediatank-function_group \
  --docker-custom-image-name <yourACRName>.azurecr.io/aimediatank-video-processor:latest \
  --docker-registry-server-url https://<yourACRName>.azurecr.io
```

## 4) Set Function App environment variables
```
az functionapp config appsettings set \
  --name aimediatank-function \
  --resource-group aimediatank-function_group \
  --settings \
  AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING="<storage-conn-string>" \
  DATABASE_URL="<postgres-conn-string>"
```

## 5) Get the Function URL
After it starts, go to **Functions → ProcessVideo → Get Function URL**.  
Use that for `AZURE_VIDEO_PROCESSING_URL` in the staging web app.

---

If you want, give me your ACR name and resource group and I’ll tailor the exact commands.
